entrant_digest_scope: sha256 of the model FILE, first 16 hex. THE ENTRANT IS THE THING BEING MEASURED, so it is identified by a digest and not by a name; `entrant` beside it is a LABEL, for reading, not for checking.
level_text:
# THE LONG CRAWL -- the retention world. This is the one the event is named for.
#
# THE KEY IS ONE ROOM FROM THE START AND THE GATE IS FOUR ROOMS AWAY, and the route to the
# gate does NOT pass back through the key's room. So the requirement has to be carried, not
# re-encountered:
#
#     hall --north--> cellar        the key is here, early, and easy to take
#     cellar --south--> hall        back out
#     hall --east--> corridor
#     corridor --north--> study
#     study --east--> vault         THE GATE
#
# An entrant that walks that route without the key arrives at a locked gate carrying nothing.
# THE FAILURE IS IN THE LOG, not in a score: the last trace row is `gate_locked` with an
# empty inventory, and `took_item_at_step` is null.
#
# The torch is a distractor: it is takeable, it is carried, and it opens nothing. Taking it is
# not an error and not a penalty -- it simply is not the item the gate wants.
#
# Verified solvable:  north ; take key ; south ; east ; north ; east      (6 commands)
# Verified UNSOLVABLE without taking the key: the same route minus the take ends `gate_locked`.

start hall

room hall Dusty Hall
desc hall A dust-choked hall. A cold draught comes from the north.
room cellar Root Cellar
desc cellar A root cellar. Damp brick, and something metal on a shelf.
room corridor Long Corridor
desc corridor A corridor running east to west, longer than the house should allow.
room study Abandoned Study
desc study An abandoned study. A vault door is set into the east wall.
room vault The Vault
desc vault The vault. The door has no handle, only a keyhole.

exit hall north cellar
exit cellar south hall
exit hall east corridor
exit corridor west hall
exit corridor north study
exit study south corridor
exit study east vault
exit vault west study

item brasskey cellar
alias brasskey key

item torch hall
alias torch lantern

gate vault brasskey

simulator_digest_scope: sha256 of the SIMULATOR FILE, first 16 hex. THE SIMULATOR IS THE INSTRUMENT THIS EVENT IS MEASURED WITH, and it is pre-registered: a record that cannot say which simulator scored it cannot be placed against the frozen criteria.

config.reasoning_rationale: Zork's answer is a COMMAND OF ONE TO FOUR WORDS -- `take key`, `north`, `north; look`. PREREG_zork.md states it as the reason the counters are kept apart, and the sibling cabinet measured what a thinking model does with a short-answer slot: 2314 tokens of deliberation and no commitment, because the deliberation is spent where the answer belongs. This is the short-answer case, so the setting is off. A LONG-ANSWER format would be the opposite case and would take this as a parameter rather than a constant -- this cabinet has no long-answer format in it.

reading_note.driver_rule: THE FIRST NON-EMPTY LINE, VERBATIM. Nothing is mined from prose; whether the line IS a command is the simulator's parser's decision.
reading_note.measured_frozen_parser_1: a first word of `i`/`I` is a DECLARED abbreviation for inventory, so a prose sentence opening with `I` is read as an inventory command and counted `parsed`, NOT `unparsed` -- the parser reads a command out of text that does not contain one, which is the filed RESIGN defect in the other direction
reading_note.measured_frozen_parser_2: a command with a trailing sentence is refused AS A WHOLE and counted `unparsed` (strict identity, per the prereg's boundary rule): `take the key and walk north` does not resolve
reading_note.consequence_for_a_reader: `parsed` is NOT a count of progress: it includes commands the world executed and did nothing with (inventory, look). The score is `finished`/`ending`, computed by the simulator; `carried_required_item` is the faculty flag.

attribution_scope: counted per row on trace[].attribution. `accepted` is what the world ACTED on; `rejected` is a verb this world knows, refused, with its reason; UNATTRIBUTABLE is not in the game's command language at all. Every row is attributed exactly once and every category maps back to one of the three frozen counters -- see trace[].counted_under.
scoreable_scope: A ROW WITHOUT THE COUNTS IS NOT SCOREABLE. This flag is true only when every row was attributed exactly once AND the per-row attribution sums back to the frozen counters. Records written before this axis existed carry no `attribution` and no `scoreable`, and their absence is the statement that they are not scoreable on it -- they are not repaired, rewritten or re-scored.
progress_scope: EVERY field of `progress` is computed from the parsed world and the world's state -- room count, objects moved, score and the BFS distance to the gate. NOTHING in it is parsed from the entrant's prose. The one prose-derived field in a run is `turns[].command`, which is the INPUT to the parser; see `progress_prose_only` for the full list, and `progress_field_source` for the declared provenance of every leaf -- a control in zork.py fails if a leaf appears without a declared source.
unreadable_is_the_aggregate_of: unparsed (the simulator's own counter, per command)
unreadable_scope: THE FORMAT FIELD, AND IT IS THE FROZEN COUNTER `unparsed` UNDER ANOTHER NAME. IT IS NOT A SINGLE CLAIM: it holds BOTH the commands that were refused (a verb this world knows, an argument it does not) AND the commands that were not in the language at all. A reader who wants to know which should read `attribution.unattributable`; a reader who needs the prereg's number reads this one. The two are reported and both are true; they are not two readings of one thing, they are two questions about one run.
missing_values_are_a_subset_of: a missing value is NOT inside `unreadable` here: `unreadable` counts COMMANDS the parser could not read, and a missing value is not a command at all -- the harness produced it. Both are non-answers and both are reported; they are SEPARATE because one is about the model's phrasing and the other about the ceiling.
never_started_scope: OUTSIDE the denominator (A7): a cell whose every answer was empty never started, and a rate taken over `attempted` can be improved by quitting early, so it is counted separately.
